challenges.title: Travel time, on-call duty (Pikett) and the upcoming BGAP

items.title: Travel time counts as working time
items.text: Journeys between clients are full working time — only the first journey in the morning and the last journey home count as a normal, unpaid commute (Art. 13 of Ordinance 1 to the Employment Act, ArGV 1).

items.title: Keeping enough Sundays off
items.text: At least every second Sunday must be a day off — hard to keep track of by hand with changing rounds and shifts.

items.title: The upcoming BGAP in view
items.text: The Federal Act on Working Conditions in Nursing (BGAP) — the nursing initiative — is not yet in force, but in future provides for a maximum working time of 45 hours, more advance notice in rostering and regulated compensation for on-call duty (Pikett).

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off Spitex in Switzerland
solutions.subtitle: From the automatic round to compensation for Sunday work — everything works together.

items.title: Rounds optimised automatically
items.text: Klacks plans visit routes so that journeys stay short and time windows are met — by car, bike or on foot.

items.title: Travel time recorded as working time
items.text: A round counts as working time from start to finish, minus unpaid breaks — the journeys between clients lie within it. When optimising the route, Klacks calculates them via a routing service, or as an estimate without one. Whether the first journey and the last journey home are included depends on the start and end of the round; Klacks does not recognise this automatically.

items.title: Sundays off monitored — hard-blocked in automatic planning on request
items.text: Klacks monitors Sundays off in a rolling window (e.g. every second Sunday off) and, on request, hard-blocks breaches in automatic planning (with manual planning it stays at a warning) — night shifts that run into Sunday correctly count as a working Sunday. Klacks automatically factors weekly rest days into the plan.

items.title: Qualifications factored in automatically
items.text: Every visit is assigned only to people with the matching qualification — with no manual checking at all.

items.title: Installed at your site: data stays on your servers
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure. Patient data stays on your servers — with a local AI model, no AI request goes to an external AI provider.

items.title: Klacksy understands your request
items.text: “Fill the rounds for tomorrow” is all it takes. If someone is off sick, Klacksy immediately suggests available cover.

example.title: Travel time, Sunday duty, one plan
example.text: Klacks counts the round, including the journeys between clients, as working time and monitors Sundays off in a rolling window — no manual recalculating. You can already store a minimum lead time for publishing the roster (e.g. two weeks) today; Klacks uses it to calculate when the plan must be ready — so once the BGAP comes into force, the planning basis is already in place.
